# GTE-3000 Series Industrial Smart Gateway Technical Manual

Document Number: GL-PRD-2024-017
Version: V3.2
Models covered: GTE-3000, GTE-3000S, and GTE-3000Pro
Published by the Product Department, Northline Industrial Systems Inc.

## 1. Product Overview

GTE-3000 Series is a industrial intelligent gateway launched by Northline Industrial Systems for discrete manufacturing and process industries. It is deployed between production line equipment and upper-level systems, responsible for protocol conversion, edge computing, and data cloud upload. The device adopts a fanless aluminum alloy casing design, supporting DIN rail mounting and wall mounting

.

There are three models in the series, with consistent hardware platforms, and differences mainly lie in computing power, number of interfaces, and wireless capabilities:

| Model | Processor | Memory | Storage | Ethernet Port | Serial Port | Wireless | Typical Power Consumption |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GTE-3000 | Quad-core 1.2GHz | 2GB | 8GB eMMC | 2 × Gigabit | 2 × RS485 | None | 6.5W |
| GTE-3000S | Quad-core 1.2GHz | 4GB | 16GB eMMC | 4 × Gigabit | 4 × RS485/RS232 | 4G Full Network Coverage | 9.2W |
| GTE-3000Pro | Eight-core 1.8GHz | 8GB | 64GB eMMC | 4 × Gigabit | 4 × RS485/RS232 | 5G + Wi-Fi 6 | 15.8W |

GTE-3000 is the basic model, suitable for small-scale data collection on a single production line; GTE-3000S adds 4G uplink and more serial ports, suitable for workshops without wired networks; GTE-3000Pro has local inference capabilities, allowing lightweight vision detection models to run at the edge

.

## 2. Environmental Parameters

| Project | Metric |
| --- | --- |
| Operating Temperature | -20℃ ~ +70℃ |
| Storage Temperature | -40℃ ~ +85℃ |
| Relative Humidity | 5% ~ 95%, No Condensation |
| Protection Level | IP40 (Can reach IP54 with dust cover kit) |
| Input Voltage | DC 9V ~ 36V, Standard 24V Power Adapter |
| Vibration Resistance | 5 ~ 500Hz,2Grms |
| Mean Time Between Failures | MTBF ≥ 100000 Hours |

When the installation site temperature is consistently higher than 60℃, a heat dissipation duct must be installed or the device must be moved out of the high-temperature area; otherwise, the processor will trigger frequency reduction protection, manifested as longer data collection cycles and increased data latency.

## 3. Interface Description

### 3.1 Power Interface

The left side of the device has a 3-pin Phoenix terminal, from left to right: V+, V-, PE. PE is the protective grounding; grounding is mandatory when there is significant electrical interference in the workshop, otherwise RS485 communication is prone to checksum errors.

### 3.2 Ethernet Ports

LAN1 is default as management port, with factory IP 192.168.1.10, subnet mask 255.255.255.0. LAN2 is default as business port, with factory configuration as DHCP client

LAN2 is default as business port, with factory configuration as DHCP client. LAN3 and LAN4 of GTE-3000S and GTE-3000Pro can be configured as switch ports, cascading downstream devices

When the management port IP is forgotten, hold the RESET button for more than 10 seconds to restore factory settings, returning the management port IP to 192.168.1.10. Restoring factory settings will clear all collected point configurations; make sure to export the configuration file before operation.

### 3.3 Serial Ports

RS485 uses a 2-pin terminal with A and B lines. Serial port parameters support 1200 ~ 115200bps, default 9600bps, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit, no parity check. A maximum of 32 slave devices can be connected on the same 485 bus, with 120Ω terminal resistors required at both ends of the bus. GTE-3000S and GTE-3000Pro have built-in terminal resistors that can be enabled via a dip switch.

### 3.4 Digital Input/Output

GTE-3000Pro provides 4 routes DI and 2 paths DO. DI is inputted for dry interfaces, which are relay output, contact capacity 30VDC/2A. DO is often used to connect sound alarms and to export signals when collecting breaks or threshold limits

. DO is often used for connecting sound alarms to export signals when collecting breaks or thresholds.

## 4. Protocol Support

Protocols supported by the device facing field equipment:

- Modbus RTU / Modbus TCP
- OPC UA Client
- Siemens S7(S7-200 Smart / S7-1200 / S7-1500)
- Mitsubishi MC Protocol (3E Frame)
- Omron FINS
- Mitsubishi FX Series Programming Port Protocol
- CNC Equipment's FOCAS Protocol (Only supported by GTE-3000Pro)

Protocols supported by the device facing upper-level systems:

- MQTT 3.1.1 / MQTT 5.0, supporting TLS encryption and mutual certificate authentication
- HTTP / HTTPS Active Reporting
- OPC UA Server
- Standard access to AWS IoT and Azure IoT platforms

GTE-3000 can be configured with up to 2000 data points, GTE-3000S with 5000, and GTE-3000Pro with 20000. New data points beyond the point limit will be rejected, and the web configuration page will prompt "Number of data points exceeds the current model limit"

New data points beyond the point limit will be rejected, and the web configuration page will prompt "Number of data points exceeds the current model limit"

## 5. Data Collection and Reporting Mechanism

Collection tasks are organized by "Collection Groups." A collection group includes several data points, a collection cycle, and a reporting strategy. The minimum collection cycle is 100ms, maximum 3600s. Reporting strategies include three types:

**Periodic Reporting**: Pack the latest value and report it at fixed intervals, independent of the collection cycle configuration. Suitable for trend data, such as temperature, current.

**Change Reporting**: Report only when the value changes beyond the set deadband threshold. Suitable for state data, significantly reducing traffic. Deadband threshold supports absolute value and percentage formats.

**Hybrid Reporting**: Immediately report upon change, while also reporting once at a longer heartbeat cycle to ensure the upper system receives the latest value even if it missed the change event. Recommended for production environments.

Data is stored in local cache when the network is down. GTE-3000 has a cache capacity of 100,000 entries, GTE-3000S has 500,000, and GTE-3000Pro has 5,000,000. After network recovery, data is resent in chronological order, with a default transmission rate limit of 200 entries per second to avoid overwhelming the upper system. When the cache is full, the oldest data is discarded on a first-in-first-out basis.

## 6. Edge Computing

GTE-3000Pro supports running edge rules and lightweight models on the device

.

## 6. Edge Computing

GTE-3000Pro supports running edge rules and lightweight models on the device.

Edge rules are written using a SQL-like syntax, for example:

```text
SELECT device_id, temperature
FROM stream
WHERE temperature > 85
```

After a rule is triggered, three types of actions can be initiated: reporting alarm messages, setting DO outputs, and calling write commands to downstream devices.

Model inference supports ONNX format, with model files not exceeding 200MB. Typical scenarios include initial screening for product appearance defects, filtering out clearly qualified images at the edge to only upload suspected defective images to the central system for re-examination, reducing upward bandwidth usage by over 80%.

## 7. Web Configuration Interface

Access `https://192.168.1.10` via browser, default account admin, default password Gl@2024. Password must be changed upon first login, with new password at least 10 characters, including at least three of the four categories: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters

.

Main functional areas:

- Runtime Monitoring: CPU, memory, storage usage, real-time status of each collection group
- Device Management: Adding, deleting, modifying, and querying field devices and data points, supporting Excel batch import
- Data Forwarding: Configuration and topic mapping for northbound connections
- Edge Rules: Rule writing and debugging
- System Maintenance: Firmware upgrades, configuration import/export, log download, time synchronization

Exported configuration files are in an encrypted .glcfg format. During import, the model and version are validated, and cross-model imports are rejected. Configurations from GTE-3000 can be imported into GTE-3000S, but not vice versa, due to the possibility of exceeding the lower model's data point limit with higher model data points.

## 8. Security Mechanism

The device defaults to disabling Telnet and FTP, only opening HTTPS and SSH. SSH default port is 22, which can be modified in the system maintenance page.

Supports three levels of user roles: administrators can perform all operations; maintenance personnel can view monitoring, download logs, and restart collection tasks, but cannot modify point configuration; visitors have read-only access.

Firmware packages are signed by Northline Industrial Systems, and signature verification is performed during device upgrades. If the signature is invalid, the upgrade is rejected and the original firmware is retained. The upgrade process takes about 3 to 5 minutes, during which data collection is interrupted. After upgrade, the device automatically restarts and restores the original configuration

The upgrade process takes about 3 to 5 minutes, during which data collection is interrupted. After upgrade, the device automatically restarts and restores the original configuration

## 9. Typical Deployment Methods

**Single Machine Deployment**: One GTE-3000 connects to a PLC and instruments on a production line, and connects to the workshop switch via LAN2, with data reporting to the plant-level MES.

**Dual Machine Hot Standby**: Two GTE-3000S units are interconnected via a heartbeat line. The standby unit takes over within 5 seconds if the main unit fails. Point configuration is automatically synchronized from the main unit to the standby unit. Hot standby requires both devices to have the same model and firmware version.

**Cascade Deployment**: At the workshop level, multiple GTE-3000 units collect data nearby, and the data is aggregated to a GTE-3000Pro for edge computing and unified cloud upload, reducing the number of public network connections.

## 10. Selection Recommendations

- Less than 500 points, with wired network, no edge computing needs: GTE-3000
- 500 to 3000 points, no network cables on site, requires 4G uplink: GTE-3000S
- More than 3000 points, requires edge inference or CNC device connection: GTE-3000Pro

The point configuration format of all three devices is fully compatible. When upgrading from GTE-3000 to GTE-3000Pro later, export the configuration and import it directly, without needing to re-enter the points.

GTE Series Gateway Field Installation and Maintenance Guide

Document Number: GL-OPS-2024-009

Version: V2.6

Models covered: GTE-3000, GTE-3000S, and GTE-3000Pro

Prepared by: Technical Service Department

1. Preparation Before Operation

Before on-site operation, three confirmations must be completed: first, confirm that the ambient temperature at the installation location does not exceed 60°C long-term, and is away from strong interference sources such as inverters and large power contactors; second, confirm that the on-site power supply is DC 9V to 36V, and an independent circuit breaker is reserved; third, confirm the network conditions, wired access requires pre-laid network cables, and 4G/5G access requires confirmation that the signal strength on-site is no less than -95dBm.

List of Tools:

2. Installation steps

1. Disconnect the on-site power supply, confirm the power indicator light is off before proceeding with wiring work.

2. Insert the gateway's snap hook into the DIN rail, first hang the side then push down to secure, you can hear the snap hook in place sound; for wall mounting, use M4 screws to fix the four corners.

3. Connect power supply: the 3-pin terminal from left to right is V+, V-, PE, PE must be connected to the grounding busbar of the cabinet, grounding resistance should not exceed 4Ω.

4. Connecting to RS485: A connects to A, B connects to B, 120Ω terminal resistor is enabled at both ends of the bus, and the shield is grounded at one end

.

5. Connect Ethernet: LAN1 is the management port, LAN2 is the business port, after the network cable is done, use the tester to confirm the wiring order is T568B.

6. Install the antenna for the wireless model, the antenna should be extended as much as possible outside the metal cabinet, installation inside the cabinet will cause signal attenuation of more than 10dB.

7. Power on, observe the indicator lights: PWR constantly lit indicates normal power supply, SYS flashing once per second indicates normal system operation, COM flashing indicates data transmission and reception on the serial port.

3. Commissioning and acceptance

Laptop network port configured as 192.168.1.100/24, access https://192.168.1.10 via browser to log in to the Web interface, default account admin, default password Gl@2024, password must be changed upon first login.

Complete sequentially: change the management port IP to the planned on-site address, configure the business port network, add southbound devices and points, configure northbound MQTT connection, start the collection group, confirm the status of each collection group is running on the operation monitoring page.

Acceptance criteria:

4. Daily maintenance

Monthly maintenance: Check indicator light status, check if CPU and memory usage on the Web interface are consistently above 80%, check if remaining storage space is below 20%, export and archive operational logs.

Qualitative maintenance: clean dust on the device surface and heat sink, retighten power and serial port terminals, check if system time deviation exceeds 1 minute, and export a complete configuration file backup

.

Annual maintenance: Check if the power adapter output voltage has decayed, evaluate if the firmware version needs to be upgraded, perform a master-slave switch exercise for dual-machine hot standby devices.

5. Common on-site fault handling

PWR light not lit: First measure the input voltage at the terminal, check the upstream circuit breaker and wiring if no voltage, if voltage exists but the device does not light up, replace the power adapter.

SYS light flashing rapidly: System anomaly, first power off and reboot; if still flashing rapidly after reboot, export logs and contact technical service department.

COM light not flashing: No data transmission on the serial port, troubleshoot in the order of A/B wiring reversed, parameter inconsistency, slave station address error, missing terminal resistor.

Collection group reports ERR-5021: Position configuration is incompatible with the protocol stack, commonly occurs after firmware upgrade across major versions, rollback firmware and reupgrade according to the transitional version.

Device frequently reboots: Troubleshoot in the order of stable power supply, environmental temperature exceeding 60°C, number of edge models exceeding 3.

6. Safety precautions

Do not connect wires while powered on; must work after disconnecting and testing for electricity.

Wear anti-static wristband before disassembling the motherboard, hold the motherboard edges, do not touch chip pins.

Use safety harness for high-altitude work, use insulating ladder for cabinet top installation.

After completing the job, count the tools to prevent metal tools from being left in the cabinet, causing short circuits

Northline Industrial Systems GTE Series Firmware Upgrade and Release Notes

Document number: GL-PRD-2024-023
Version: V1.8
Models covered: GTE-3000, GTE-3000S, and GTE-3000Pro
Maintenance Department: Product Department Firmware Group

I. Firmware Version Naming Convention

Firmware version numbers are in the format 3.2.14-r5, with the following four segments:

3   Major version number, incremented when there is a major hardware platform change or protocol stack restructure
2   Minor version number, incremented when new features are added
14  Revision number, incremented when defects are fixed
r5  Release batch, re-packaging of the same revision number with no functional changes

| Firmware with different main version numbers cannot be directly upgraded, for example, from 2.x to 3.x must first upgrade to transition version 2.9.20, then to 3.0.0. Jump version upgrade will cause configuration files to be unreadable, and all points will be lost after device boot |

.

II. Current Maintenance Versions

3.2.14-r5   Stable version, released in September 2024, recommended for production environments
3.3.6-r2    Feature version, released in December 2024, supports 5G dual SIM dual standby and MQTT 5.0
2.9.20-r8   Maintenance version, only fixes critical defects, maintenance stops on December 31, 2025

III. Major Changes in 3.3.6

New Features:
1. MQTT 5.0 support, supports shared subscriptions and topic aliases, reducing message overhead by about 15% in long connection scenarios
2. GTE-3000S and GTE-3000Pro support 5G dual SIM dual standby, automatically switching to the backup SIM within 30 seconds when the main SIM fails
3. Collection groups support importing and exporting to Excel, including fields such as point name, register address, data type, and scaling coefficient
4. Web interface adds a "Communication Quality" panel, displaying response time and timeout rate for each southbound device
5. Edge rules support window functions, allowing calculation of 5-minute sliding averages

Bug Fixes:
1. Fixed the occasional frame loss issue with RS485 at 115200bps over long periods, caused by the serial port driver buffer not being cleared in high load conditions
2. Fixed the data order disorder issue during disconnection recovery, with the recovery queue now strictly sorted by timestamp
3. | Configuration file import fixes DO |

2. Fixed the data order disorder issue during disconnection recovery, with the recovery queue now strictly sorted by timestamp
3. Fixed the issue where DO output status was not reset after importing a configuration file
4. Fixed the issue where OPC UA Server did not release sessions after abnormal client disconnection, rejecting new connections after exceeding 64 sessions
5. Fixed the issue where log timestamps were set to 1970 when the device time was not synchronized

Known Issues:
1. GTE-3000Pro has high memory usage when running more than four ONNX models simultaneously, suggesting no more than three models per device
2. FOCAS protocol connection to some older FANUC systems is slow on the first handshake, taking about 20 seconds

IV. Pre-upgrade Preparation

1. Export the current configuration from the Web interface under [System Maintenance] → [Configuration Management], with the filename recommended to include a date, for example line3-gw01-20241220.glcfg
2. Export the last 7 days' logs from [System Maintenance] → [Log Download], for comparison after upgrade
3. Ensure the device power supply is stable, as power interruption during upgrade may damage the firmware, requiring factory re-flashing
4. Verify that the current firmware version matches the target firmware version's major version number
5. Notify relevant production line personnel that data collection will be interrupted for 3 to 5 minutes during the upgrade

Five, Upgrade Operation Steps

Method One: Web Interface Upgrade (Recommended)

1. | Access device management via browser |

| 3 to 5 minutes |

Five, Upgrade Operation Steps

Method One: Web Interface Upgrade (Recommended)

1. Access the device management port https://192.168.1.10 via a browser and log in with an administrator account
2. Navigate to [System Maintenance]→[Firmware Upgrade]
3. Click "Select File" and upload the .glfw firmware package
4. The system automatically verifies the signature and model compatibility. Once verification is successful, the "Start Upgrade" button becomes clickable
5. Click "Start Upgrade", the page displays a progress bar. At this time, do not close the page or power off the device
6. After the progress reaches 100%, the device automatically restarts. The Web interface will be accessible again approximately 60 seconds later
7. After logging in, check the version number in [Operation Monitoring] to confirm it has been updated, and ensure all collection groups are in "Running" status

Method Two: Batch Upgrade

| Use Northline Industrial Systems device management platform for batch deployment when more than 20 devices |

. The platform pushes firmware in groups, supporting batch gray release: first upgrade 10% of devices, observe 24 hours without anomalies, then push the remaining devices.

Six, Handling Upgrade Failures

Phenomenon One: After uploading the firmware package, it prompts "Signature Verification Failed"
The cause is that the firmware package is incomplete or from an untrusted source. Redownload from the official channel and verify the SHA256 checksum

Phenomenon Two: Prompt "Model Mismatch"
The firmware package for GTE-3000 and GTE-3000S is not interchangeable. Check the model identifier in the package name

Phenomenon Three: The device is inaccessible after the upgrade
First confirm whether the management port IP has changed. Access 192.168.1.10 directly. If still inaccessible, hold RESET for 10 seconds to restore factory settings, then import the configuration file exported before the upgrade

Phenomenon Four: The collection groups do not run after the upgrade, and the log shows ERR-5021
This is due to incompatibility between the point configuration and the new version protocol stack, commonly seen when upgrading from 2.x to 3.x. Roll back to the version before the upgrade, and reupgrade through the 2.9.20 transitional version

Seven, Firmware Rollback

Devices retain the firmware image of the previous version. Click "Rollback to Previous Version" on the [System Maintenance] → [Firmware Upgrade] page. The rollback process takes approximately 2 minutes. Only one historical version is retained. After two consecutive upgrades, rollback to an earlier version is not possible.

. Only one historical version is retained. After two consecutive upgrades, rollback to an earlier version is not possible.

After rollback, the configuration file will automatically downgrade to be compatible, but new configuration items in the new version will be lost, for example, when rolling back from 3.3.6 to 3.2.14, the 5G dual-card configuration and window function rules will be cleared

Employee number, consecutive characters. Passwords must be changed every 90 days, and new passwords must not be the same as the previous 5 times.

### Q11: How to troubleshoot RS485 communication timeout

?

Follow the steps below to troubleshoot:

1. Confirm that the A and B lines are not reversed; reversed connections result in no response at all.
2. Confirm that the serial port parameters match those of the slave device, especially the baud rate, data bits, stop bits, and parity.
3. Confirm that the slave address is correct, with Modbus slave address ranging from 1 to 247.
4. Confirm that 120Ω terminal resistors are connected at both ends of the bus, and they must be connected if the distance exceeds 300 meters.
5. Confirm that the device's PE terminal is grounded. In environments with many variable frequency drives, interference is strong, and grounding is essential to prevent data loss.
6. Use the [Running Monitoring]→[Communication Quality] panel to check the response time and timeout rate to determine if the issue is with all slaves or individual slaves.

### Q17: What should I do if I forget the Web management password?

Guest password cannot be recovered, so the device must be reset via factory reset. Operator and visitor account passwords can be reset by the administrator via [System Maintenance]→[User Management]. It is recommended to retain at least two administrator accounts during deployment.

### Q18: What security reinforcement measures does the device support?

Data will not be immediately lost. When the network is disconnected, data is stored in local cache. GTE-3000 can cache up to 100,000 entries, GTE-3000S up to 500,000 entries, and GTE-3000Pro up to 5,000,000 entries

The data is automatically retransmitted once the network is restored. Only when the cache is full and the network is still not restored will the oldest data be discarded on a first-in-first-out basis

### Q19: Does the firmware upgrade automatically?

No. The device does not perform automatic upgrades. All upgrades must be manually triggered via the Web interface or device management platform to avoid unexpected interruption of data collection during production hours.
